title: NZ Gym Etiquette
meta_desc: Learn unwritten rules of NZ gym etiquette, including weight rack, machine wipe, headphones and personal space to make the most of your workout
intro: New to the gym scene in New Zealand? Knowing the unwritten rules of gym etiquette is essential to ensure a smooth and enjoyable workout experience for both you and others. From racking your weights to respecting personal space, we've got you covered. In this guide, we'll explore the essential dos and don'ts of gym etiquette in NZ and provide you with practical tips to make the most of your gym time.

sections.heading: Rack Your Weights
sections.body: One of the most important rules of gym etiquette is to rack your weights after use. This not only helps keep the gym floor tidy but also prevents accidents and injuries. Most NZ gyms, including City Fitness and Les Mills, provide designated weight racks for you to store your weights. Make sure to put your weights back in their original place after your workout, and don't leave them on the floor.
list: Always rack your weights after use
Don't leave weights on the floor

sections.heading: Wipe Down Machines
sections.body: Wiping down machines after use is essential for maintaining gym hygiene and preventing the spread of germs. Most NZ gyms provide disinfectant wipes or sprays for you to clean the equipment after your workout. Jetts and Anytime Fitness are two gym chains that emphasize the importance of cleaning equipment after use.

sections.heading: Headphones and Personal Space
sections.body: When working out, it's essential to respect other people's personal space. Wear headphones to listen to music or podcasts, and avoid disturbing others who may be working out nearby. Be mindful of your surroundings and keep a safe distance from others, especially during peak hours.
list: Wear headphones to listen to music

sections.heading: Peak Hour Tips
sections.body: Peak hours at the gym can be challenging, especially if you're a beginner. To make the most of your workout during peak hours, plan your routine in advance, and be prepared to adjust your schedule if needed. Consider working out during off-peak hours or taking advantage of group fitness classes, which are often less crowded.
list: Be prepared to adjust your schedule
Consider off-peak hours or group fitness classes

sections.heading: Specific NZ Gym Cultures
sections.body: Different NZ gym chains have unique cultures and rules. For example, some gyms may have specific rules around grunting or dropping weights, while others may have a more relaxed atmosphere. Familiarize yourself with the gym's rules and culture before your workout, and be respectful of other gym-goers.
list: Familiarize yourself with gym rules and culture
Follow specific rules around grunting or dropping weights

sections.heading: Get Started with the Right Gym
